features.description: Element measurement and focus tracking. New elements/ category (created by this batch). Observer mocks + disconnect-on-dispose tests.
features.name: Elements: size, visibility, focus
features.evidence: All seven shipped. Batch A: useMutationObserver. Batch B: useResizeObserver + useIntersectionObserver. Batch C: useElementVisibility, built on the shipped useIntersectionObserver. Batch D (2026-10-04): useElementBounding + useFocus + useFocusWithin, which complete the feature and the elements/ category. The four observers stay the native thing with nothing wrapped: options alias the platform init type (MutationObserverInit / ResizeObserverOptions / IntersectionObserverInit), callbacks are the platform's verbatim, and one $effect creates the observer per run and disconnects on replacement or unmount. Deliberate non-abstraction: the three observers share ~20 lines of effect scaffolding but unifying them would force one lowest-common-denominator return shape (pause/resume for intersection, takeRecords for mutation, neither for resize), so each stays self-contained. isSupported is a plain boolean - no useSupported (feat-025, niche) exists. useIntersectionObserver inlines pause/resume/isActive as $state rather than adding a usePausable primitive that is not on the roadmap, and its resume() is a no-op after stop(), which VueUse's unconditional isActive = true would get wrong. Two VueUse behaviours deliberately not reproduced, both documented in the READMEs: useElementVisibility's `once` option registers a watchOnce inside the observer callback, so it stops after the SECOND report rather than the first its docstring promises (untested upstream) - this implementation compares against the previous value and stops on the first change, which also means the unconditional report the platform makes on observe() does not consume it; and useElementVisibility returns a bare ShallowRef by default plus a controller under a `controls` flag - here `stop` is always returned, so there are two shapes to collapse into one. Option properties accept `| undefined` because the package compiles with exactOptionalPropertyTypes, so a Svelte `let rootMargin = $state<string>()` forwards straight through. No deprecated local observer types, no instanceof Element filter (that would reject Text nodes and depends on a global constructor check). Consolidated the inline observers whose ponytail markers asked for it: useScroll observe.mutation and useTextareaAutosize width-change; both call sites' existing tests already spy MutationObserver.prototype / MockResizeObserver, so the swaps are proven by them passing unchanged. useElementHover's inline observer watches document, not an element, and stays inline by design. jsdom ships MutationObserver so Batch A drives the real thing; jsdom has no ResizeObserver/IntersectionObserver so Batches B and C use the existing test/fixtures/observers.ts mocks, which gained a multi-entry `trigger` so the latest-entry-wins rule is testable. Batch D: useElementBounding composes useResizeObserver + useMutationObserver rather than re-implementing either, and additionally watches window scroll in the CAPTURE phase plus window resize, because a scroll can move the box without resizing it (a sticky ancestor, a transformed subtree) and neither observer fires for that; updateTiming 'next-frame' defers a burst of reports into one read. Two VueUse options dropped as no-ops: `immediate`, which VueUse accepts and never reads. useFocus returns one getter/setter pair instead of VueUse's WritableComputedRef plus focus()/blur() methods - the two methods are the two assignments, and a bare `ShallowRef` is the wrong shape for Svelte. useFocusWithin uses relatedTarget containment instead of VueUse's `:focus-within` re-check, which is stale by construction: focusout is dispatched BEFORE focus moves, so the pseudo-class still describes the old focus and the flag sticks on; its `focused` is read-only because imperative focus belongs to useFocus. Both focus utils type the target as MaybeGetter<MaybeHTMLElement> (new shared alias) rather than MaybeElement, because focus()/blur() and the FocusEvent event map only exist on HTMLElement - that is what lets useEventListener's HTMLElementEventMap overload hand back a typed FocusEvent instead of a cast. shared/is.ts gained isNode() for that reason too: relatedTarget is typed EventTarget | null but is always a Node, a Window, or null, and `'nodeType' in value` narrows without instanceof (which misses iframe nodes) and without a cast. The useFocus initialValue effect calls el.focus() directly instead of through the accessor, since going through the setter would make the effect read the $state it writes and loop. useElementBounding's public update() is a no-op under SSR - caught by its own SSR probe, which is the only reason that probe exists. Tests: 13+4, 15+3, 18+4, 16+3, 12+4, 14+3, 9+2. Gates: check 0/0, format clean, lint 0 errors 0 warnings, test 960/960 across 105 files, prepack publint clean, consumer probe, rune scan and path-leak scan clean.

features.description: Document/page-level visibility, icon, fullscreen. (useTitle skipped: <svelte:head> covers it.) All SSR-guarded with server fallbacks.
features.evidence: Batch A (2026-10-04): all three functions, closing the feature. useWindowFocus and usePageLeave take no options at all: upstream ConfigurableWindow is dropped, since the only window worth watching is the one the code runs in and there is nothing to configure. useFullscreen kept autoExit and dropped ConfigurableDocument. One upstream bug fixed in usePageLeave: VueUse points all three listeners at one handler doing isLeft = !event.relatedTarget, so re-entering the page fires mouseenter with a nullish relatedTarget and sets isLeft back to true - the pointer just arrived and the flag says it left (it self-corrects on the next move between elements). mouseenter gets its own handler here, pinned by a test that dispatches the null-relatedTarget case explicitly. useFullscreen uses ONLY the standard Fullscreen API: VueUse probes twenty prefixed spellings across four name tables (webkitRequestFullScreen, mozCancelFullScreen, msExitFullscreen, ...), and every browser that shipped one has shipped the unprefixed version since ~2011, while TypeScript lib.dom types only the unprefixed four - so the tables bought compatibility with browsers that cannot run a modern Svelte app, at the cost of string-indexed lookups this package forbids (no casts). The one live prefixed form, webkitEnterFullscreen, is video-only on iPhone and belongs to native <video controls>. That deleted roughly half the upstream implementation and with it four @ts-expect-error suppressions. Two more upstream readings changed, both in the README: isSupported asks only whether requestFullscreen and exitFullscreen exist, because the fullscreenEnabled flag upstream also requires is a PERMISSION bit (an iframe without allowfullscreen reports false while both methods are present), and isFullscreen compares document.fullscreenElement against the target. Upstream resolves a fullscreenEnabled-style property NAME and reads that as the state, which was right for webkitIsFullScreen ("is in fullscreen") but not for the standard fullscreenEnabled ("is fullscreen allowed") - so on any current browser VueUse reports isFullscreen true whenever the API is merely available, and exit() then refuses to run because it is gated on that flag. Kept faithful: a fullscreenchange naming a different element is ignored (another component fullscreen is not this flag business); the initial sync runs in its own $effect, because folding it into the autoExit effect would run the teardown on every target change and exit fullscreen when a bind:this target rebinds; and enter() sets the flag optimistically once the request resolves, leaving fullscreenchange to keep it honest. jsdom implements none of the Fullscreen API, so the tests stub requestFullscreen/exitFullscreen/fullscreenElement with Object.defineProperty and delete them in afterEach. 36 jsdom tests + 7 SSR probes across the three (useFullscreen 20+3, usePageLeave 9+2, useWindowFocus 7+2), closing feat-018. Suite 1199/1199 across 123 files; init.ps1 all green.
features.name: Document & page UI

features.description: Touch/drag interactions and outside/long-press handlers. (useDraggable reopened as real scope: a zero-dep port of VueUse's element/handle dragging, shipped alongside @neodrag/svelte rather than deferring to it; useParallax moved to feat-026 — needs useDeviceOrientation + useScreenOrientation.) features.name: Gestures & drag
features.evidence: Batch A: onClickOutside + onLongPress (the feature's last two T1 functions). 52 tests across 4 files. Three upstream defects fixed, each with a red test first: (1) onClickOutside cancel() was erased by the pointerdown preceding the click it was meant to swallow - now a separate swallowNext flag, so it is usable from a pointerdown handler; (2) onLongPress onMouseUp stayed silent when a press was abandoned for drifting past the threshold, because the cancel path erased the start position - onMove now cancels only the timer, so a drag still reports isLongPress: false; (3) modifiers.once no longer uses a native once listener, so an abandoned first press no longer leaves the element deaf forever. onClickOutside returns a fixed { stop, cancel }; controls / trigger / detectIframe and the iOS < 13.4 listener rewrite are deliberately not ported (README documents why). Batch B: useDraggable. 35 jsdom tests + 3 SSR probes. Two design notes: autoScroll is not ported (a 60fps interval, a four-knob option object, and a per-frame position correction - a feature bundled into a drag util rather than part of dragging; the README gives the onMove equivalent), and draggingElement falls back to window when nullish rather than binding nothing, because a nullish element in Svelte usually means a target that has not resolved yet. One hand-rolled bind instead of useEventListener, because passive is fixed at bind time and preventDefault must keep working when switched on. No casts and no DOM instanceof: Element/EventTarget do not carry the pointer event map, so the handlers take Event and narrow with a 'pointerId' in event predicate, the same trick useMouse uses. test/fixtures/rect.ts added (stubRect + stubScroll), replacing the copy useElementBounding kept locally. Batch C: usePointer. 31 jsdom tests + 4 SSR probes. Three deliberate deviations, all documented in the README: pointerType is typed string rather than 'mouse' | 'pen' | 'touch' (the DOM types it as string because a device may report its own name, and VueUse's union only holds via a cast - widening it also makes pointerTypes: ['eraser'] compile); a named target that resolves to nullish binds nothing rather than falling back to window, deliberately the opposite of useDraggable, because here the fallback would report pointers the caller never asked about (and target: undefined still means the default); and the upstream @default ['mouse','touch','pen'] on pointerTypes is not honoured, because upstream ships no filter and a port that filtered by default would silently drop events. isInside is set before the type filter, matching upstream - a filtered-out pointer still counts as inside, which is the useful order. isPointerEvent moved from useDraggable to shared/is.ts (it would have been the third copy) and test/fixtures/pointer.ts grew tiltX/tiltY/width/height/twist. Suite 1085/1085 across 113 files; init.ps1 all green (lint 0 problems). Batch D: useSwipe. 36 jsdom tests + 3 SSR probes, and a refactor the port needed first: bindListener moved out of useEventListener into useEventListener/bind.ts (internal, not re-exported, so it stays out of the barrel) because useSwipe has to hold the detachers for stop() and read passive at bind time - useDraggable's private bind() went with it. isMouseEvent/isTouchEvent joined isPointerEvent in shared/is.ts (deleting three private copies: useMouse had two, useScrollLock one), Position moved to shared/types.ts with useDraggable re-exporting it so the public surface is unchanged, and test/fixtures/pointer.ts gained touchEvent(). One real bug the tests caught: threshold as its own $derived caches, so a getter returning a new threshold was silently ignored forever - it is now read inside the derived that depends on the diffs, which is the only moment it matters. Simplifications: upstream's `capture && !passive` guard is just `!passive` (capture is defined as !passive), and upstream's stop() over useEventListener return values cannot be ported literally because our useEventListener returns void. touchend deliberately does not reset the coordinates, so direction survives the lift and is still readable in onSwipeEnd. Public type names follow upstream exactly (UseSwipeDirection, and coordsStart/coordsEnd typed Readonly<Position>), which is why the exported type is UseSwipeDirection rather than a shorter SwipeDirection. Suite 1124/1124 across 115 files; init.ps1 all green. Batch E: useDropZone. 29 jsdom tests + 3 SSR probes. Zero deps - reuses useEventListener for the four drag events. jsdom has no DragEvent and no DataTransfer, so isDragEvent (new in shared/is.ts, needed because the target union includes Document, which leaves the listener handlers typed as Event) guards on 'dataTransfer' in event, and test/fixtures/pointer.ts gained dragEvent() and dropFile() to build a MouseEvent carrying a structural dataTransfer. dataTypes is deliberately NOT a MaybeGetter, unlike every other option in this package: a function there already means the validation predicate, so a getter for the list could not be told apart from it - checkValidity is the reactive escape hatch, read per event, and takes precedence over both dataTypes and multiple. files is $state.raw because the contents are File objects. Two upstream behaviours reproduced rather than fixed, both documented in the README: multiple: false REJECTS a multi-file drop outright, so the [files[0]] truncation is unreachable until a custom checkValidity has approved the drop (a test pins that), and Safari is detected by user agent because it exposes items but not files during a drag, which would make every dataTypes check fail there. One upstream bug fixed: an unbalanced dragleave drives the counter negative in VueUse, after which counter === 0 is never true again and isOverDropZone sticks on forever - clamped at zero, with a test. Target is HTMLElement | Document | nullish, re-resolved per effect run, so useEventListener removes and re-adds the listeners on rebind and no stale closure survives; nullish binds nothing rather than falling back to window, because a document-wide zone nobody asked for would swallow every drop on the page. Suite 1156/1156 across 117 files; init.ps1 all green.

features.description: The only two items promoted out of the svelte-base sweep, both qualifying under scope.md §3. useId: ids must match between the server render and hydration, which is a genuine env-branching problem (3.2), and every util that needs an id depends on it (3.4). Implement on top of $props.id() where a component is available; the module counter + Math.random() form in svbase is NOT portable as written (module-scope mutable state, scope.md §2, plus non-stable across server/client). README documents $props.id() as the first choice for component-level ids. useControllableState: non-trivial reactive state (internal value overridden by an external prop, with a setter) that core lacks and that useToggle/useCounter/useStorage each re-invent; Svelte has no controlled/uncontrolled primitive. Kept as a building block (3.4).
